procedure: Listen to the teacher’s explanation of system dynamics and how the simulation will be implemented.
Open the online simulation tool on a computer or tablet.
Manipulate different variables in the simulation, changing one variable at a time.
Observe and record how the system reacts to each change.
Use an S-curve to review the results.
Discuss how changes impact the entire system and how its parts are integrated and balanced.
aim: To understand how variability affects a system by manipulating variables in an interactive simulation and reviewing the results using an S-curve.

viva.question: What is a system?
viva.answer: A set of connected parts that interact to achieve a purpose or produce an outcome.

viva.question: What does system dynamics study?
viva.answer: How a system’s behaviour changes over time as its parts interact.

viva.question: What is a variable in a simulation?
viva.answer: A factor that can be changed to observe its effect on the system.

viva.question: What does an S-curve show?
viva.answer: How a system quantity changes over time, often showing slow, rapid, and then slower growth.

viva.question: Why should you change one variable at a time?
viva.answer: So you can identify which change caused the observed system response.

viva.question: What is meant by balance in a system?
viva.answer: The interacting parts of the system remain in a state where their effects are managed or offset.

diagram: Draw an S-shaped curve with the vertical axis labelled “System quantity” and the horizontal axis labelled “Time”; label the curve’s sections “slow growth,” “rapid growth,” and “levelling off.”
title: Interactive Simulation of System Dynamics
precautions: Use a trusted simulation tool and follow the teacher’s instructions.
Change one variable at a time so its effect can be identified.
Record the settings and observations clearly for each change.
Use the same time interval when comparing simulation results.
Handle the computer or tablet carefully and keep it away from liquids.
result: The simulation showed that changing variables affects the behaviour of the system over time. Reviewing the results with an S-curve helped identify changes in the system’s growth and balance.
